hints: Kruskal processes edges in increasing weight.
An edge is excluded from every MST if its endpoints are already joined by strictly lighter edges.
Test all equal-weight edges before merging any of them.
analogy: At each weight, see which endpoints are already connected by cheaper roads before considering ties.
example: In a triangle with weights 1,2,3, the weight-3 edge cannot occur in an MST; the other two can.
algorithm: Sort edges by weight. For each equal-weight group, first mark an edge YES exactly when its endpoints are in different disjoint-set components formed by lighter edges. Then union all edges of the group. Print answers in input order.
correctness: If lighter edges already connect the endpoints, the edge is uniquely heavier on a cycle and cannot appear in an MST. Otherwise it can be chosen first among equal-weight edges in Kruskal's algorithm and extended to an MST.
complexity: For n vertices and m edges, O(m log m+m alpha(n)) time and O(n+m) space.
